title: Computational Workflow for Genome-Wide DNA Methylation Profiling and Differential Methylation Analysis
author: Pei-Yu Lin
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Run initial quality control
steps.instruction: Assess raw read quality with FastQC using the command `fastqc wt_r1.fastq`; examine the generated reports `wt_r1_fastqc.html` and `wt_r1_fastqc.zip`. Use a Phred score cutoff of <20 or <30 to flag low‑quality bases.

steps.title: Remove duplicates and trim adapters
steps.instruction: Remove PCR duplicates with BS‑Seeker2’s FilterReads.py (`./BSseeker2/FilterReads.py -i wt_r1.fastq -o wt_r1_rmdup.fastq > FilterReads.log`) and then trim adapters and low‑quality reads with TrimGalore (`./TrimGalore/trim_galore --fastqc_args "--outdir ./qc_trimming" wt_r1_rmdup.fastq`). The final cleaned FASTQ file is `wt_r1_rmdup_trimmed.fq`.

steps.title: Download Arabidopsis reference genome
steps.instruction: Download the TAIR10 genome from iGenomes with `wget https://s3.amazonaws.com/igenomes.illumina.com/Arabidopsis_thaliana/NCBI/TAIR10/Arabidopsis_thaliana_NCBI_TAIR10.tar.gz` and extract it using `tar -xzvf Arabidopsis_thaliana_NCBI_TAIR10.tar.gz`. The fasta file is located at `./Arabidopsis_thaliana/NCBI/TAIR10/Sequence/WholeGenomeFasta/genome.fa`.

steps.title: Build Bowtie2 index for reference
steps.instruction: Create a Bowtie2 index for BS‑Seeker2 with `bs_seeker2-build.py -f genome.fa --aligner=bowtie2 -d ./BS2_bt2_Index` (where `genome.fa` is the TAIR10 fasta).

steps.title: Align trimmed reads to reference
steps.instruction: Map the cleaned reads to the Arabidopsis genome using BS‑Seeker2: `bs_seeker2-align.py -i wt_r1_rmdup_trimmed.fastq -g genome.fa --aligner=bowtie2 -o wt_r1_align.bam`.

steps.title: Call methylation and create CGmap
steps.instruction: Generate cytosine‑level methylation calls with `bs_seeker2-call_methylation.py -i wt_r1_align.bam -o wt_r1.CGmap -d /BS2_bt2_Index/genome.fa_bowtie2`. The output is a gzipped CGmap file (`wt_r1.CGmap.gz`).

steps.title: Inspect CGmap file
steps.instruction: View the CGmap content using `zless wt_r1.CGmap.gz`; each line lists chromosome, Watson‑strand nucleotide, position, context (CG/CHG/CHH), dinucleotide context, methylation level, #C (methylated), and #C+#T (total).

steps.title: Build lambda genome index for conversion rate
steps.instruction: Create a Bowtie2 index for the unmethylated lambda genome with `bs_seeker2-build.py -f lambda_genome.fa --aligner=bowtie2 -d ./BS2_lambda_Index`.

steps.title: Align reads to lambda genome
steps.instruction: Map the original reads to the lambda reference using `bs_seeker2-align.py -i wt_r1_rmdup.fastq -g lambda_genome.fa --aligner=bowtie2 -o wt_r1_lambda.bam -m 3 -d BS2_lambda_Index`.

steps.title: Call methylation on lambda alignment
steps.instruction: Run `bs_seeker2-call_methylation.py -i wt_r1_lambda.bam -o wt_r1_lambda -d BS2_lambda_Index/genome.fa_bowtie2/` to obtain `wt_r1_lambda.CGmap.gz`.

steps.title: Calculate bisulfite conversion rate
steps.instruction: Execute the R script `Rscript coversion_rate.R wt_r1_lambda.CGmap.gz` (available at https://github.com/beritlin/NGS_analyses/blob/main/DNA_Methylation_Analyses/coversion_rate.R). The script computes conversion rate = (#T / (#T + #C)) × 100 and prints the percentage (e.g., 97.01%).

steps.title: Create samples list for MethylC‑analyzer
steps.instruction:
Generate a tab‑separated file `samples_list.txt` with columns: sample name, CGmap file, group name. Example lines:
`wt1	wt1.CGmap.gz	WT`
`wt2	wt2.CGmap.gz	WT`
`wt3	wt3.CGmap.gz	WT`
`met1_1	met1_1.CGmap.gz	met1`
`met1_2	met1_2.CGmap.gz	met1`
`met1_3	met1_3.CGmap.gz	met1`.

steps.title: Run MethylC‑analyzer DMR detection
steps.instruction:
Execute the Docker command:
`docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/app peiyulin/methylc:V1.0 python /MethylC-analyzer/scripts/MethylC.py DMR samples_list.txt gene.gtf /app/-a met1 -b wt`
Default parameters: minimum read depth per CpG `-d 4`, qualified sites per region `-q 4`, region size `-r 500 bp`, p‑value cutoff `-pvalue 0.05`, methylation difference `-dmrc 10%`. The command produces `DMR_CG_all_0.1.txt`, `DMR_CG_hyper_0.1.txt`, and `DMR_CG_hypo_0.1.txt`.

steps.title: Create sample file for HOME
steps.instruction:
Prepare `sample_file.tsv` (tab‑separated) with group name followed by all CGmap files for that group. Example:
`wt	wt1.CGmap.gz	wt2.CGmap.gz	wt3.CGmap.gz`
`met1	met1_1.CGmap.gz	met1_2.CGmap.gz	met1_3.CGmap.gz`.

steps.title: Run HOME DMR detection
steps.instruction:
Run the HOME tool:
`HOME-pairwise -t CG -i sample_file.tsv -o ./ -mc 4 --BSSeeker2`
Defaults: minimum sites per region `-mc 4`, minimum region length `-ml 50 bp`, methylation difference `-d 10%`, classifier score cutoff `-sc 0.1`, pruning cutoff `-p 0.1`. Output files are per‑chromosome DMR lists such as `HOME_DMRs_1.txt`.

steps.title: Generate BigWig from BAM
steps.instruction:
Create a BigWig track for visualization with deepTools:
`bamCoverage -b wt_r1_align.bam -o wt_r1.bw`.

steps.title: Visualize data in IGV
steps.instruction: Use IGV desktop to view methylation tracks.

substeps.instruction: Convert WIG to BigWig via Tools > Run IGVtools if needed.
Load tracks (File > Load) such as `wt_r1.bw` and CGmap‑derived BED files.
Navigate to a chromosome/region using the dropdown or search box; zoom with +/- controls.
Save the session or export an image (File > Save Session / Save Image).

steps.title: Perform enrichment analysis
steps.instruction:
Run MethylC‑analyzer Fold_Enrichment:
`docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/app peiyulin/methylc:V1.0 python /MethylC-analyzer/scripts/MethylC.py Fold_Enrichment samples_list.txt gene.gtf /app/-a met1 -b wt`
Outputs include `CG_Fold_Enrichment.pdf` and BED files such as `CommonRegion_CG.txt.bed`.

steps.title: Conduct metagene (metaplot) analysis
steps.instruction:
Execute:
`docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/app peiyulin/methylc:V1.0 python /MethylC-analyzer/scripts/MethylC.py Metaplot samples_list.txt gene.gtf /app/-a met1 -b mt`
Generates `metaplot_CG.pdf`, `metaplot_delta_CG.pdf`, and BigWig files (e.g., `met1_r1_CG.bw`).

steps.title: Identify differentially methylated genes
steps.instruction:
Run the DMG module:
`docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/app peiyulin/methylc:V1.0 python /MethylC-analyzer/scripts/MethylC.py DMG samples_list.txt gene.gtf /app/-a met1 -b wt`
Outputs include text and BED files for hypo‑ and hyper‑DMRs and associated genes.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in several plant and human studies. Approaches from read alignment to methylation calling were applied in Hsieh et al. [43,44], Lin et al. [30], Hossain et al. [45], and Lu et al. [21]. The DMR identification step was also used in Hsieh et al. [43,44] and Lin et al. [30] with different criteria. This protocol (or parts of it) has been used and validated in the following research articles: Hsieh et al. [43]. Epigenetic factors direct synergistic and antagonistic regulation of transposable elements in Arabidopsis. Plant Physiology (Figure 2E). Lin et al. [30]. Estimating genome-wide DNA methylation heterogeneity with methylation patterns. Epigenetics & Chromatin (Figures 2, 3, and 4). Hsieh et al. [44]. Rice transformation treatments leave specific epigenome changes beyond tissue culture. Plant Physiology . Lu et al. [21]. MethylC-analyzer: a comprehensive downstream pipeline for the analysis of genome-wide DNA methylation. Botanical Studies .
